note: Issue #161. Shared golden corpus that pins the Go answer (api/internal/termsafe.Unsafe)
and the web answer (web/src/lib/safeText.ts stripUnsafeChars, regex /(?![\n\t])[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}]/gu)
to ONE agreed classification, so the two independent implementations cannot silently drift.
termsafe.Unsafe(r) == unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf) == category Cc||Cf.
'unsafe' is that predicate's verdict. Both test suites load THIS file and assert their own
predicate agrees with 'unsafe' for every code point below; a change to either implementation
that disagrees with a listed code point reds that side's test.
Code points are HEX STRINGS (no U+ prefix), never literal characters, so this file carries no
raw control/format/NUL bytes (a literal NUL would make git treat it as binary; a literal bidi
override would reorder this file in an editor). Both loaders parse cp as base-16.
\n, \t and \r are deliberately ABSENT: they are Cc (unsafe by this predicate) yet SPARED by
the sanitizers' whitespace exception, so listing them here would conflate the category predicate
with a sanitizer's policy. Whitespace-sparing stays covered by each side's own behaviour tests.
U+FFFD is listed as SAFE (category So): it is not Cc/Cf, so the predicate passes it. That records
that handler.validateSecretLabel's separate `r == unicode.ReplacementChar` reject is an EXTRA test
on top of the shared predicate, not part of it.
